column1: # Issue 0653 — the ONE table both router resolvers answer.
# `scripts/dev/zenohd.sh` (`nros_zenohd_bin`, used by `just <plat> zenohd`) and
# `nros_tests::process::ros_zenohd_path` (used by the test harness) must resolve
# the same router: a contributor debugging a lane by hand and the lane itself
# have to start the same process. Neither can call the other — one is shell, one
# is Rust — so the guarantee has to come from somewhere, and a comment saying
# "the two must agree" was what there was. They drifted anyway.
# So: one table, two consumers.
#   * `scripts/check-zenohd-resolution-parity.sh` runs the SHELL over it.
#   * `zenohd_resolution_matches_the_shared_table` runs the RUST over it.
# A row is written once and answered twice; a resolver that disagrees fails on
# its own side, naming the row.
# Each row is decided by a DIFFERENT step of the order, and each would be
# answered wrongly by some plausible alternative order — a table where every row
# is settled by step 1 proves nothing about steps 2..5.
# COLUMNS  name <TAB> explicit <TAB> path <TAB> ament <TAB> distro <TAB> optros <TAB> expected
# `@` is the synthetic root each runner creates; `$rel` is
# `lib/rmw_zenoh_cpp/rmw_zenohd`. An empty `expected` means BOTH resolvers must
# FAIL — a fallback path here would turn "no router" into a spawn error several
# frames from the cause (issue 0599).
# Prefixes each runner materialises under `@`, all holding an executable router:
#   @/overlay  @/underlay  @/optros/humble  @/optros/jazzy  @/bin/rmw_zenohd
#   @/explicit/router     @/nothing (created EMPTY — no router)
# `optros` is the conventional root steps 4 and 5 search, a column rather than a
# constant so the last row can say "no router anywhere" at all. Both runners
# pass it as NROS_ZENOHD_OPT_ROS, which is the only reason that override exists.
